findings.text: Charged page returns are coalesced per group in a small per-CPU associative cache. Oversize returns or lock contention bypass the cache and uncharge directly. Cached totals that grow beyond the configured batch trigger eviction of that entry. Misses with no free slot evict in round-robin order. Eviction uncharges the accumulated total and releases the group reference.
Batch ceiling MEMCG_CHARGE_BATCH is build-time constrained to not exceed S8_MAX, keeping per-slot page tallies in a byte-sized field.

Memory accounting always releases the main memory counter, and additionally releases the combined memory-plus-swap counter only when legacy swap accounting is enabled. One configuration determines enablement from hierarchy mode, another configuration disables it unconditionally.

Kernel memory statistic updates distinguish normal execution from non-maskable interrupt context. Normal context uses the regular per-CPU statistic path. Interrupt context instead marks scheduler statistics as updated on the current processor and adjusts a central atomic tally. An alternate build always uses the regular path regardless of context.

A public state adjustment entry accepts a group, a statistic selector, and a signed delta. It is inert when the controller is disabled, otherwise it resolves the nearest non-dying ancestor under read-side protection and applies the delta to per-CPU storage while refreshing aggregated accounting and emitting a trace event.

Object-charged byte returns are staged per processor per object group. Whole pages translate back to the owning memory group for kernel memory release, while sub-page remainders fold into a centralized per-group byte total for later batching. Kernel memory release adjusts the kernel statistic negatively, invokes a legacy hook that is inert in the observed build, and skips page-counter release for the root group. Accounted size includes an extra pointer for group membership. Draining the slot that owns pending slab-category totals also flushes those totals and clears the association.

The observed page stock carries a lock, a small fixed-size association array keyed by group, a parallel array of narrow page tallies, and a round-robin eviction cursor. The observed object stock carries a parallel association array, a byte tally array, an index identifying which slot owns pending slab-category totals, a node identifier, and separate accumulators for reclaimable and unreclaimable slab bytes.

Page-stock mutation is guarded by a per-CPU local lock acquired opportunistically without waiting; failure takes a direct uncharge path that needs no stock access. Slot association and tally fields use single-access ordered primitives for concurrent observation. Object-stock draining assumes exclusive ownership of the slot being cleared and orders association publication similarly.

Slab location services form a chain: a slab yields a node number through its descriptor flags and section mapping, and the node number yields the node data structure for accounting. The section-to-node translation is served by a table lookup keyed by section derived from flags.

Object extension storage places the owning object group first when present, so retrieval and installation are direct field accesses without offset computation. Both operations assert that the slab actually requires group accounting.

The slab byte-category selector maps a cache to one of two node byte counters based solely on whether the reclaim-account flag is set, directing later byte accumulation to the reclaimable or unreclaimable total.

Object release follows a veto pipeline with an outcome indicating whether the caller may proceed to reuse the memory. Debug ownership checks, fenced allocation handling, and sanitizer pre-checks can veto reuse. An optional initialization request clears object and metadata regions while preserving red-zone and original-size information. A final sanitizer outcome determines reuse eligibility, with type-safe reclamation potentially deferring the actual free. One observed group-accounting free hook variant performs no action.

Object layout distinguishes whether the free link lives inside or outside the usable area by comparing link offset against in-use length. Debug original-size storage, when enabled for kmalloc caches with user-store debugging, resides after the usable area plus link space and two tracking records, with fenced addresses resolved through a dedicated size query.

Slab release occupancy governs list membership. Debug and tiny configurations always return through the partial-list path. Otherwise freelist and usage are updated atomically with retries; transitions involving full-to-partial or any-to-empty acquire node list synchronization. Empty slabs beyond the configured partial minimum are removed when previously partial and then discarded with node totals decremented, while newly non-full slabs join the tail.

Freelist publication uses an atomic double-word update where the platform supports it, otherwise it serializes comparison and installation under interrupt-disabled bit-spin protection of a dedicated flag with single-store publication of the counter half. Contended updates back off briefly and count a failure statistic. Node list changes are serialized by the owning node list lock with interrupt state preserved.

Free-link storage is an offset-based slot within or adjacent to the object. Hardened builds obscure the stored link by mixing the cache random value and a byte-reversed slot address, and reject self-referential links as corruption. Unhardened builds store the link directly.

Slab discard decrements node slab and object totals in one configuration and is inert in another. Debug release validates trailing padding and every object when consistency checking is enabled, honoring poison filling and accounting for extension areas that may live inside the slab. Type-safe caches defer backing release through deferred reclamation, others release immediately.

Slab extent is a power-of-two multiple of the base page size determined by the folio order. Object iteration strides by cache object size across the object count from a red-zone-adjusted start. Extension footprint is either an aligned trailing region sized by per-object extension size or identically zero with out-of-slab indication, depending on configuration.

Slab diagnostics emit distinct bug and fix message families with cache identity and taint state, dump affected padding regions as hex, and record slab identity including object counts, usage, freelist, and flags. Corrupted padding is restored to the poison pattern after reporting. Under unit-test capture, error counting and taint suppression replace console escalation.

Externally reachable services in these fragments include group statistic adjustment, section-to-node translation, object-release validation, and unit-test membership probing. Each tolerates inert or negative outcomes: disabled controller, absent test context, or missing named test resource.

Key hazards include lost batching under stock contention, duplicate release or link corruption masked without hardening, atomic update livelock under persistent contention, misattributed statistics for dying groups or wrong nodes, sanitizer-quarantined reuse assumptions, and silent padding corruption without poison checking.
Negative one for index and NUMA_NO_NODE for node act as empty sentinels after flush.
An iteration abstraction walks each object in a slab by advancing a cursor over the object count with cache stride from an adjusted base, exposing each element address to the caller body.
